title: Pratap Singha and the Reorganisation of Power
content: Accession of Susenghphaa/Pratap Singha and the priorities of the reign.
Momai Tamuli and other leading administrators; the evolution of the Borbarua and Borphukan offices.
Reorganisation of labour, settlements, provincial administration, and military command.
Royal policy towards religious institutions and the changing political economy.
Court politics, frontier policy, succession, and the limits of claims assigning every institution to one reformer.
visual: An administration chart distinguishing earlier institutions from later reforms.

title: The First Major Ahom–Mughal War Cycle
content: Mughal expansion through Bengal, Koch Hajo, local allies, and frontier ambitions.
Campaign-by-campaign accounts of early fighting, including engagements such as Samdhara where supported.
Balinarayan and regional resistance; commanders, forts, river crossings, and supply.
Compare Ahom chronicles with Mirza Nathan’s Baharistan-i-Ghaybi and other Persian accounts.
The Asurar Ali settlement, its terms, frontier implications, and later violations.
visual: A campaign sequence and side-by-side source comparison.

title: The Short Reigns after Pratap Singha
content: Suramphaa/Jayaditya Singha and Sutingphaa: individual reign and household dossiers.
Accession, ministers, royal disputes, illness traditions, deposition, and succession.
Continuity and change in administration, religious patronage, and frontier policy.
What chronicles record and what later authors infer from sparse material.
How short reigns affected the court before Jayadhwaj Singha’s accession.
visual: A two-reign chronology with a distinction between facts and explanations.

title: Jayadhwaj Singha before the Invasion
content: Sutamla/Jayadhwaj Singha: accession, officers, household, and religious patronage.
Western expansion, Mughal weakness, Guwahati, and the disputed frontier.
Military and administrative preparations, alliances, and intelligence.
Vaishnava affiliations and the coexistence of different religious practices.
The political circumstances that preceded Mir Jumla’s campaign.
visual: A frontier map and a royal-and-ministerial profile.

title: Mir Jumla’s Invasion
content: Mughal objectives, commanders, routes, boats, artillery, and logistics.
Ahom defensive decisions, retreat, the occupation of the capital, and resistance.
Monsoon, disease, supply failure, communications, and civilian experiences.
Comparison of Ahom records, Persian narratives, and later historical writing.
Separate attested movements from dramatic reconstructions of conversations or motives.
visual: A season-by-season campaign map and logistics diagram.

title: Ghilajharighat and Ramani Gabharu
content: Treaty negotiations, payments, hostages, boundaries, and obligations as recorded in relevant texts.
The political and economic consequences for the royal household and kingdom.
Ramani Gabharu: kinship, transfer to the Mughal court, later life, and limits of the evidence.
Diplomatic correspondence and marriage as instruments of imperial politics.
Jayadhwaj’s death, succession, and how the settlement was remembered.
visual: A treaty-clause comparison and a documented biography of Ramani Gabharu.

title: Chakradhwaj Singha and the Recovery of Guwahati
content: Supangmung/Chakradhwaj Singha: accession and the decision to resist Mughal demands.
Lachit Borphukan, Atan Burhagohain, ministers, officers, and collective command.
Recruitment, shipbuilding, fortification, supplies, and the recovery campaign.
Recapture of Guwahati and rebuilding of defensive positions.
Assess royal speeches, command legends, and claims about individual responsibility against their earliest sources.
visual: A recovery campaign map and biographies of the command team.

title: Alaboi: Defeat and Its Consequences
content: Political and military pressure surrounding the confrontation.
Terrain, deployment, command choices, and the limits of tactical reconstruction.
The battle sequence and variations in casualty figures.
Consequences for strategy, morale, fortification, negotiations, and civilian communities.
How Alaboi entered memory and why defeat belongs alongside victory in a complete history.
visual: A cautious terrain reconstruction and casualty-source comparison.

title: Saraighat: War on the Brahmaputra
content: Ram Singh’s campaign, negotiations, river defences, and the strategic position of Guwahati.
Lachit, Atan, naval officers, soldiers, labourers, allies, and opposing commanders.
Land engagements, naval manoeuvres, supply, illness traditions, and battle chronology.
Udayaditya Singha’s reign during the battle and the wider political setting.
Victory, its limits, subsequent frontier developments, and the source history of famous anecdotes.
visual: A source-based battle map and an anecdote-versus-evidence panel.

title: After Saraighat: Udayaditya and Ramadhwaj
content: Sunyatphaa/Udayaditya Singha and Suklamphaa/Ramadhwaj Singha: accession, household, and officers.
Religious disputes, court coalitions, royal removals, and political violence.
Atan Burhagohain, Debera Borbarua, and competing centres of authority.
The transition from military success to succession crisis.
Explain overlap with the Saraighat chapter using cross-references instead of repeating the battle.
visual: A faction chart and two-ruler dossier.

title: Kingmakers and the Rapid Succession Crisis
content: Suhung, Gobar, Sujinphaa, and Sudoiphaa: complete short-reign sections.
Debera Borbarua, Atan Burhagohain, Laluk Sola Borphukan, and shifting alliances.
Installations, assassinations, ministerial purges, and disputed chronology.
The loss of Guwahati and its political and military circumstances.
Effects on provincial command, labour mobilisation, court trust, and ordinary inhabitants.
visual: A month-by-month sequence where dates survive and a faction-network diagram.

title: Sulikphaa, Joymoti, and Gadapani
content: Sulikphaa/Ratnadhwaj Singha and the Lora Raja tradition: accession and ruling coalition.
Treatment of royal rivals and the rules and practices surrounding eligibility for kingship.
Joymoti’s biography, Gadapani’s movements, persecution traditions, and sources for the narrative.
Noble opposition, the change of ruler, and the creation of a new political settlement.
Compare documentary accounts with later theatre, cinema, literature, and memorial culture.
visual: A historical-evidence dossier for Joymoti and a succession map.

title: Gadadhar Singha and the Battle of Itakhuli
content: Supaatphaa/Gadadhar Singha: accession and the Tungkhungia ruling line.
Restoration of command, ministerial power, labour obligations, and political stability.
The Itakhuli campaign, recapture of Guwahati, and the western frontier settlement.
Religious policy, public works, punishment, and social consequences.
Succession, assessment of the reign, and comparisons with earlier recoveries.
visual: An Itakhuli campaign map and a Tungkhungia genealogy.

title: Rudra Singha: Royal Ambition and Cultural Expansion
content: Sukhrungphaa/Rudra Singha: court, ministers, royal family, and political ambitions.
Rangpur, Joysagar, patronage, workshops, and the development of royal infrastructure.
Relations with Kachari/Dimasa, Jaintia, neighbouring rulers, and religious institutions.
Projected wider campaigns: distinguish preparation, intention, and operations actually undertaken.
Death, succession plans, court culture, and burdens of labour and expenditure.
visual: A capital-development map and a projects-and-campaigns register.

title: Siva Singha and the Bar Rajas
content: Sutanphaa/Siva Singha: accession, court, officers, and religious patronage.
Phuleswari, Ambika, and Sarbeswari: individual biographies, authority, titles, and succession.
Temples, tanks, gifts, inscriptions, royal ritual, and the organisation of patronage.
Relations with Vaishnava communities and the source history of coercion and humiliation narratives.
Connect tensions to later developments while avoiding a single-cause explanation of rebellion.
visual: A queen-by-queen dossier and patronage map.

title: Pramatta Singha: Construction and Consolidation
content: Sunenphaa/Pramatta Singha: accession, household, principal officers, and court politics.
Rang Ghar and other attributed projects: construction phases, inscriptions, materials, and function.
Continuity in regional policy, administration, religion, and labour mobilisation.
Festivities, royal display, craftsmanship, and the social costs of monumental building.
Death and succession; distinguish historical structures from later restoration.
visual: An illustrated project catalogue with dates and attribution confidence.

title: Rajeshwar Singha: Court, Campaigns, and Pressure
content: Suremphaa and Rajeshwar Singha: names, accession, household, and ministers.
Kirtichandra Borbarua and court power; evaluate traditions of chronicle suppression or destruction.
Manipur relations, campaigns, political marriages, and the position of Kuranganayani.
Palaces, temples, tanks, administration, and changing military and fiscal demands.
Religious conflict, succession, and the conditions inherited by Lakshmi Singha.
visual: A campaign-and-patronage map and a Kuranganayani biography.

title: Neighbours, Frontiers, and Long-Distance Diplomacy
content: Dedicated sections for Kachari/Dimasa, Jaintia, Koch polities, Manipur, Tripura, and relevant eastern connections.
Relations with Naga, Mising/Miri, Mishmi, Khamti, Singpho, Bhutanese, and other communities where period evidence exists.
Duar and posa arrangements, markets, gifts, tribute, marriage, envoys, and border disputes.
Frontiers as negotiated spaces: distinguish claims, influence, occupation, tribute, and administration.
Catalogue missions and agreements missed by a reign-by-reign narrative; date institutions individually.
visual: A relationship matrix and a frontier map with changing layers.
